transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-05 15:00 PST
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Marcus Lee (Aventis), Sofia Alvarez (Aventis CTO), Evan Carter (Aventis InfoSec), Priya Raman (Aventis SRE)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
- Weekly pilot sync for Aventis air-gapped POC; focused on handshake failures and intermittent routing drops.
- SE reviewed pcap and server logs; main suspects: MTU mismatch on on-prem switches + one legacy cert not rotated on bastion host.
- Agreed immediate mitigations and next steps (see action items).

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): okay everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll keep this tight 45 minutes. Quick roll call and then Priya will go through the packet captures from the two failed runs last week.
[00:18] Marcus (Aventis): hey Jordan, Marcus here, and we have Sofia, Evan, Priya R on the line. thanks.
[00:25] Priya (Redwood SE): cool, alright i'm going to share my screen but i will also narrate. i pulled the pcap from the staging bastion at 11/02 run. main symptom was a cluster of TLS handshake resumptions failing with "unexpected EOF" on the gRPC stream. you can see timestamps lining up with our ingress egress cycle.
[00:45] Priya (Redwood SE): so first observation, there are repeated TCP dup ACKs and fragmented packets, looks like mtu fragmentation around 1452 bytes in this environment which is under our recommended 1500 so something is trimming headers mid-path.
[01:05] Priya (Redwood SE): second observation - one of the bastion nodes still served an older certificate chain (CN mismatch on rotation). that causes a short-lived handshake failure which our client retries, but the retries sometimes exhaust before the KV cache prefill finishes.
[01:28] Sofia (Aventis): when you say "older cert" do you mean the system cert or the mTLS client cert?
[01:33] Priya (Redwood SE): good question, it's the server cert on the egress proxy/bastion path not the client mTLS. the client certs looked fine. the server cert on one node had a 2023-issue date, we expected 2025 rotation applied but it didn't.
[01:50] Evan (Aventis): mm-hmm that was my suspicion, our config-management pipeline skipped that host due to a tag mismatch.
[01:56] Marcus (Aventis): yeah that host was manually stood up during lab tests and missed chef run 42.
[02:05] Jordan (Redwood): ok that's helpful — so two parallel problems: network trimming (MTU) and cert rotation. Either could trigger the gRPC error chain. Which one is higher probability? Priya?
[02:16] Priya (Redwood SE): i'd say mtu fragmentation is higher probability for the bulk of failures. the pcap shows ~12% connection attempts encountering fragmentation and then seeing TLS frames split awkwardly leading to "unexpected EOF" in the library. The cert rotation explains the intermittent full handshake failures we saw that lasted ~2-3 minutes per host.
[02:38] Lena (Redwood CSM): quick clarifying q — is the fragmentation caused by your network gear or by the edge router in our colo?
[02:45] Priya (Redwood SE): could be either; our trace suggests the path MTU discovery didn't complete correctly because of an ICMP block on an intermediate firewall. So the edge router is likely blocking ICMP 'fragmentation needed' and the host keeps sending large segments.
[03:02] Priya Raman (Aventis SRE): we do have strict egress ACLs that drop ICMP. we can loosen for the pilot specifically.
[03:08] Evan (Aventis): security concern there, but we can allow the single ICMP type for the known Redwood IPs in staging.
[03:14] Jordan (Redwood): great — that would probably eliminate the fragmentation class of errors quickly. Next, cert rotation — what's the plan to reconcile that missed node?
[03:23] Marcus (Aventis): i'll trigger an adhoc config run and rotate the certs. we'll run a smoke test and paste the logs.
[03:29] Marcus (Aventis): question — is there a recommended cert TTL for air-gapped? ours currently is two years.
[03:36] Priya (Redwood SE): for pilot we recommend shorter TTL in staging (6 months) to catch rotation issues earlier; production you can align with your compliance. also we support SIGHUP-based reloads so we don't need full restarts for most proxies.
[03:51] Jordan (Redwood): quick note on fallback routing — we observed on 11/02 that when the bastion egress fails, the client retried and eventually attempted a fallback to hosted Redwood endpoints; that path worked but latency jumped. p99 went to ~420ms versus target 120ms.
[04:10] Priya (Redwood SE): yes the fallback worked as intended but the KV prefill semantics change slightly when you cross from private to hosted: keys are not warmed and you get cold-start tokenization overhead. we saw tokenization add 60-90ms per request.
[04:25] Sofia (Aventis): is there any data leakage risk when falling back to hosted? we have tight PD controls.
[04:32] Jordan (Redwood): good flag — in the pilot fallback test we were using masked inputs and PII-scrubbed payloads; full enterprise deployments can opt out of automatic fallback and instead fail closed. We also documented the data flows in the security deck. i'll send the section.
[04:47] Evan (Aventis): we will need explicit guarantees and a short matrix of which workloads can fallback — apis that touch PHI must not.
[04:54] Jordan (Redwood): understood — we'll produce a fallback gating doc and include SSO/KMS notes.
[05:00] Priya (Redwood SE): another subtlety — kernel scheduling differences. we ran an experiment bumping from 5.15 to 5.19 on one node; that removed a context-switch regression but introduced 8-12% higher CPU sys for the grpc worker thread. it reduced the long-tail latency failures but increased head CPU which could trigger autoscaler thrashing in small clusters.
[05:28] Marcus (Aventis): we observed that — our autoscaler did spike and started preempting pods unexpectedly.
[05:34] Priya (Redwood SE): right — so mitigation options: 1) tune kernel throttling parameters + set cpuset for GRPC workers, 2) keep kernel at 5.15 and instead tune socket buffer sizes, or 3) increase pool size and accept higher baseline CPU. We recommended option 1 for pilot.
[05:55] Priya Raman (Aventis SRE): option 1 sounds ok but we need a maintenance window. Also need rollback plan if autoscaling triggers.
[06:03] Jordan (Redwood): we'll coordinate that. Lena, can you help schedule with Marcus?
[06:07] Lena (Redwood CSM): yes i'll ping Marcus and get 2 candidate windows next week.
[06:12] Priya (Redwood SE): quick note on observability — i'll upload a trimmed pcap + annotated notes. link: https://redwood.app/pilot/aventis/pcap-1102 (internal). Marcus, please confirm you can access.
[06:23] Marcus (Aventis): i can access. nice.
[06:26] Priya (Redwood SE): one more test suggestion — run a controlled cert-rotation while capturing tcpdump and ensure no ICMP blockage. that will validate both root causes in one go.
[06:40] Marcus (Aventis): good plan, we'll test tomorrow in staging.
[06:44] Sofia (Aventis CTO): on compliance, Evan will collect artifacts. Jordan, can you attach SOC2 related docs for pilot?
[06:51] Jordan (Redwood): yes i'll attach the current SOC2 self-attestation and the network segmentation notes to the pilot thread after the call.
[06:57] Evan (Aventis): also, does Redwood support HSM-backed keys in private? we need that for encryption-at-rest proof points.
[07:04] Jordan (Redwood): yes — for Private deployments we support KMS/HSM integrations (customer-managed). we'll share the integration checklist.
[07:12] Priya (Redwood SE): small gotcha i want to call out — our client library will consider a connection "dead" after 3 attempts by default; for air-gapped flaky networks you may want to bump retry policy to 6 and add 200ms jitter to avoid thundering herd during rotation windows.
[07:33] Marcus (Aventis): ok we'll test increasing retries.
[07:36] Jordan (Redwood): any other open questions?
[07:39] Priya Raman (Aventis SRE): one more — the bastion logs show some repeated TLSv1.2 fallbacks. can Redwood enforce TLS 1.3 only?
[07:47] Priya (Redwood SE): by default our runtime prefers TLS1.3 and we can drop TLS1.2 on the egress proxy, but it depends on client compatibility. for the pilot we can enforce TLS1.3 between your bastion and the Redwood private edge.
[08:00] Evan (Aventis): sounds good. we'll check client libs.
[08:04] Jordan (Redwood): recap of next steps: Priya to upload pcap + notes, Marcus to run cert rotation test and paste logs, Jordan to send SOC2 and fallback gating doc, Lena to propose maintenance windows. We'll reconvene after artifact uploads or in the next weekly slot.
[08:22] Jordan (Redwood): thanks everyone — we'll follow up in the pilot channel.
[08:26] Sofia (Aventis): thanks all. bye.
